title: Hárman megyünk: How Many of Us?

sections.title: A number for a group of people
sections.content: When you say how many people are in a group, you use a special form of the number ending in *-an/-en*: *kettő* ("two") becomes *ketten*, *három* becomes *hárman*. It means "the two of us/you/them" and needs no noun. The verb agrees with the people, so it is plural: *Hárman megyünk moziba* ("The three of us are going to the cinema"). The question is *Hányan vagytok?* ("How many of you are there?"). The ending is *-an* after back vowels and *-en* after front vowels.

items.english: The three of us are going to the cinema.
How many of you are there? – There are four of us.
Many people are coming to the party.

sections.content: *kettő*, *három* and *kevés* change their stems (*ketten*, *hárman*, *kevesen*); the others just add the ending. Compare *három barát jön* ("three friends are coming", with a noun) with *hárman jönnek* ("the three of them are coming", no noun). You will also meet *mindketten* ("both of them") in a later unit.
